title: Azure Storage Queue Depth and Poison Messages

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `azure:monitor:metric` events with `resource_type="microsoft.storage/storageaccounts" metric_name="QueueMessageCount"` into `index=cloud`. Confirm UC-4.2.56 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `azure:monitor:metric` traffic without `resource_type="microsoft.storage/storageaccounts" metric_name="QueueMessageCount"`. Confirm UC-4.2.56 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=cloud` sourcetype=`azure:monitor:metric` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics); validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.storage/storageaccounts" metric_name="QueueMessageCount"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.56_azure_storage_queue_dept_56"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.2.56 — Azure Storage Queue Depth and Poison Messages: queries Microsoft Azure `azure:monitor:metric` for search criteria `resource_type="microsoft.storage/storageaccounts" metric_name="QueueMessageCount"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for performance review and change validation.
value: On Microsoft Azure, detecting 'Azure Storage Queue Depth and Poison Messages' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.2.56 drives high-priority performance alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Collect Azure Monitor metrics for Storage Account queue services. Monitor `QueueMessageCount` for growing backlogs and `QueueCapacity` for storage limits. Set up a separate alert for poison queues (queues ending in `-poison`) with any messages. Alert when main queue depth exceeds baseline by 3x or poison queue is non-empty.
visualization: Line chart (queue depth over time), Single value (current depth), Table (queues with poison messages).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.storage_free_percent) as free_pct
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.Storage
  by Performance.host span=1h
| sort 10 free_pct
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (Storage node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=cloud`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics) with the modular input for `azure:monitor:metric`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.2.58.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect Azure Monitor metrics for Storage Account queue services. Monitor `QueueMessageCount` for growing backlogs and `QueueCapacity` for storage limits. Set up a separate alert for poison queues (queues ending in `-poison`) with any messages. Alert when main queue depth exceeds baseline by 3x or poison queue is non-empty.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=cloud sourcetype="azure:monitor:metric" resource_type="microsoft.storage/storageaccounts" metric_name="QueueMessageCount"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.2.56_azure_storage_queue_dept_56"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `azure:monitor:metric` in `index=cloud` to detect azure storage queue depth and poison messages. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_2_56_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (queue depth over time), Single value (current depth), Table (queues with poison messages)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` (Azure Monitor metrics) and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure storage queue depth and poison messages so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
